# Registration and number plates {#sec-dd-registration}

```{r}
source("R/book.R")
cols <- dict_groups$registration
cs <- coverage_share(cols)
dd <- read_pipeline("outputs", "data_dictionary.csv")
n_miss <- setNames(dd$n_missing, dd$column_name)
tf <- read_coverage("true_by_first_use_year")
cov_vanity <- function(y) {
  x <- tf[tf$column_name == "vanity_plate" & tf$first_use_year %in% y, ]
  fmt_pct(x$n_true / x$n_vehicles, 0)
}
```

## Overview

The registration mark, or number plate, is the only identifier the sources
share, and the key used to link them (@sec-sources-linkage).

- **`registration_DVSA`** is the plate as supplied in the DVSA MOT history.
  It is the plate the vehicle carried when the data was extracted, which may
  not be the one it was first registered with.
- **`registration_DVLA`** is the plate returned by the DVLA Vehicle Enquiry
  Service (VES) for this vehicle. It usually matches the DVSA plate; where it
  does not, the plate has moved to another vehicle, and `dvla_match`
  (@sec-dd-dvla-status) says whether the VES record can be trusted.
- **`registration_clean`** is the DVSA plate upper-cased with spaces and
  punctuation removed. Use it for joins.
- **`registration_at_first_test`** is the plate the vehicle carried at its
  first MOT test, as supplied by the Bristol team. It differs from
  `registration_DVSA` where the plate has changed since, for example to a
  cherished plate. The pipeline carries it through without using it.
- **The `plate_` columns** decode the plate's format: its type (current
  style, prefix, suffix, dateless and others), the period in which a plate of
  that form was issued, and the issuing office or region.
- **`vanity_plate`** is `TRUE` where the vehicle's birth date falls outside the
  plate's issue period. This flags cherished plates, but also imports, Q plates
  and other re-registered vehicles.
- **`plate_ever_changed_VES`** is `TRUE` where the registration returned a
  different vehicle between VES lookups.

The plate formats and their meaning are explained in @sec-number-plates, and
the decoding rules in the methodology,
[section 6.2](../../reports/methodology.md#number-plate-decoding).

::: {.callout-important title="Registrations are personal data"}
Registration marks can identify a vehicle's keeper when combined with other
information. The conditions for using them are set out in @sec-data-products.
:::

```{r}
#| label: tbl-dd-registration
#| tbl-cap: "Registration and number plate columns."
dict_table("registration")
```

## Coverage

The DVSA registration, and everything decoded from it, is present for every
vehicle. The plate's issue dates are blank only for the
`r fmt_n(n_miss["plate_date_from"])` vehicles whose plate has no dated period,
and `vanity_plate` is blank where either the plate period or the birth date is
missing.

The DVLA registration and `plate_ever_changed_VES` are present wherever a VES
lookup was made: `r cov_pct(cs, "registration_DVLA")` of all vehicles. The
lookups were made for every DVSA registration between 2024 and 2026, so they cover
almost every vehicle first used up to 2022, fewer of those first used since
(`r cov_year("registration_DVLA", 2025)` for 2025), and almost none of
those first used in 2026, which were registered after the lookups were made
(@fig-dd-registration).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-dd-registration-coverage
#| tbl-cap: "Share of vehicles with a value, by year of first use."
coverage_table(cols)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-dd-registration
#| fig-cap: "Share of vehicles with a DVLA registration, by year of first use."
#| fig-height: 2.6
coverage_plot("registration_DVLA", ncol = 1)
```

`vanity_plate` is almost never blank, but the share of vehicles flagged
varies a good deal with age (@fig-dd-vanity), from about
`r cov_vanity(1995)` of vehicles first used in 1995 to
`r cov_vanity(2018)` of those first used in 2018. Take this into account
before reading the decoded plate period or location as the vehicle's own.

```{r}
#| label: fig-dd-vanity
#| fig-cap: "Share of vehicles whose plate does not match their age (vanity_plate TRUE), by year of first use."
#| fig-height: 2.6
coverage_plot("vanity_plate", ncol = 1, flags = TRUE)
```

## Values

How the values of each column change over time, by year of first use, from 1990. Numeric columns and
dates show the minimum, lower quartile (Q1), median, upper quartile (Q3) and
maximum; other columns show the share of vehicles with each value, with the
less common values grouped as *All other values* and missing values as
*Blank*.

```{r}
#| output: asis
cat(dict_values("registration"))
```
